Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: "Allonymous" cells: retrospective capture of the pre-drug primed state
ideas.description: Barcode an isogenic population and use a sister-cell split design (Rewind/ClonMapper-style) so that survivors' barcodes can be traced back to their untreated twins, which are then profiled by scRNA-seq. This measures the cell state that existed before drug exposure, distinguishing pre-existing priming from drug-induced reprogramming.

ideas.title: "Indelibly": measuring the memory half-life of the resistant state
ideas.description: Isolate primed or persister cells, culture them drug-free for intervals from hours to weeks, and re-challenge at each time point to build a decay curve of resistance probability. The decay rate, compared to the division rate, reveals whether the state is a transient fluctuation or a heritable epigenetic memory.

ideas.title: "Insulator": stochastic chromatin boundary loss at resistance driver loci
ideas.description: Combine single-cell ATAC/CUT&Tag with Micro-C or 4C at loci such as AXL, NGFR, or MET in primed versus naive cells, then CRISPRi the implicated CTCF/cohesin boundary elements. This tests whether rare survival arises from sporadic loss of insulation that permits ectopic enhancer-promoter contact.

ideas.title: "Sync": signaling and cell-cycle phase at the moment of drug addition
ideas.description: Image cells carrying ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters plus a PIP-FUCCI cell-cycle sensor continuously through drug addition and for days afterward, linking each cell's pre-treatment dynamics to its fate. This asks whether survival is determined by the timing and phase of signaling pulses, a dynamic cause invisible in fixed-cell snapshots.

ideas.title: "Mesh": survival as a property of the local cellular neighborhood
ideas.description: Use micropatterned islands, controlled seeding densities, and tunable-stiffness substrates, together with spatial transcriptomics of residual disease, to quantify how neighbor contacts, local density, and matrix mechanics predict persistence. Non-random spatial clustering of survivors would show that the rare state is partly environmental rather than cell-intrinsic.
